title: gonk images are amd64-only but the cluster is mixed-arch; any reschedule to an arm64 node breaks the deploy
description:
OUTAGE 2026-07-31 ~02:23 UTC. gonk-meter is in CrashLoopBackOff with 'exec /usr/local/bin/gonk-meter: exec format error'.

CAUSE: orac is a mixed-architecture cluster --
  johnny  amd64   (kaniko builds run here, so images are amd64)
  venus   amd64
  bailey  arm64
  orac01-04 arm64
5 of 7 nodes are arm64. The gonk images are built single-arch amd64 by the homelab kaniko template on johnny. The chart exposes intake/meter/controller nodeSelector, tolerations and affinity (chart/gonk/values.yaml:94,121,252) but ALL default to {} -- nothing constrains gonk workloads to amd64. The deployment has only ever worked because the scheduler happened to place pods on johnny/venus.

TRIGGER: the chart version embeds the git SHA (gonk-0.1.0+<sha>), so ANY commit to main causes Flux to cut a new chart release and recreate pods -- rolling the dice on architecture each time. Commit 5dcd286 (a beads/gitignore-only commit) was enough. gonk-meter landed on orac04 (arm64) and could not exec.

CASCADE: helm upgrade timed out waiting for gonk-meter + gonk-intake to become Ready; Flux's automatic rollback to gonk.v5 timed out for the same reason; the release is now stuck STATUS=pending-rollback at revision 8. gonk-intake is 0/1 Ready, controller has restarted 5x. dolt is unaffected because dolthub/dolt-sql-server is a multi-arch upstream image.

FIX, two options:
 (a) Constrain scheduling: set nodeSelector {kubernetes.io/arch: amd64} for intake/meter/controller. Cheapest, honest about what the images actually are. Correct home is arguably the Flux HelmRelease values in the gitops repo (deployment-specific), not the chart defaults -- pinning arch in the chart would become wrong the day images go multi-arch.
 (b) Build multi-arch images (kaniko --customPlatform / buildx equivalent, or a manifest list). Bigger job, owned by homelab/ci-templates (project 65), but it is the durable answer on a 5-of-7 arm64 cluster.

Recommend (a) now to restore service, (b) as the real fix.
design: Note the interaction with the chart's Recreate strategy and the etcd-write-sensitive upgrade caveat already recorded on gonk-dxo. Also note that a stuck pending-rollback release blocks further Flux reconciliation, so restoring service needs the release unwedged (helm rollback to a good revision, or a forced upgrade) IN ADDITION to the scheduling constraint -- a nodeSelector alone will not un-stick revision 8.
acceptance_criteria: gonk-intake, gonk-meter and gonk-controller are Running and Ready, the HelmRelease reports READY=True, and a pod-delete test confirms rescheduling cannot land a gonk workload on an arm64 node.
close_reason:
RESOLVED and verified live. The outage is over: ns gonk runs v0.1.0-d0443ac159e7 on multi-arch images, HelmRelease Ready=True UpgradeSucceeded, all four pods Running with 0 restarts, meter healthy. The wedged pending-rollback release cleared itself once working images existed -- no manual helm rollback was needed.

Durable fix was multi-arch images (gonk-owi.1) rather than pinning gonk to the 2 amd64 nodes, so a reschedule onto any of orac's 5 arm64 nodes is now survivable and no nodeSelector is required. Unblocked by homelab/ci-templates!1 and !2 (rootless native per-arch kaniko legs + crane manifest merge).

title: [bug] gonk-gate envArg uppercased param names -> every dispatch arg empty, no formula ever poured
description: cmd/gonk-gate/main.go's envArg read GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_<UPPERCASE(name)>, but Gas City sets GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_<name> with the [order.params] key verbatim (internal/webhookmatch/extract.go ExecEnvVars is a plain map copy over declared param names). Every gonk param is lower_snake_case, so every arg read back empty and gonk-dispatch failed with 'unknown trigger; pouring nothing' trigger="" -- after meter had already been asked, so it burned a budget decision and poured nothing.

title: gonk-meter LiteLLM adapter broken against real v1.92.0: spend poller (v2 date format + response envelope + pagination) and admin update-by-alias (/key/info)
description:
Found by Plan 06 L2 (test/component: first contact between internal/meter/litellm and a REAL LiteLLM ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.92.0). Two independent, reproducible, FATAL defects. The adapters were written against docs + httptest mocks (which returned the WRONG shape), so both slipped through Plan 03.

=== BUG A (spend poller, FATAL) -- internal/meter/litellm/spendsource_http.go ===
Meter can NEVER ingest spend against real v1.92.0 => never synced => Ready() never true => every budgeted /decide defers forever.
1. fetchPage sends start_date/end_date as time.RFC3339 ("2026-07-01T00:00:00Z"). Real /spend/logs/v2 rejects it: HTTP 400 {"message":"Invalid date format: 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z. Expected: 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'"}. FIX: format as "2006-01-02" (or "2006-01-02 15:04:05").
2. Since() does json.Unmarshal(body,&entries) with entries []logEntry, but v2 returns an OBJECT {"data":[...],"total","page","page_size","total_pages"}, NOT a bare array. Even with dates fixed, unmarshal fails. FIX: decode {"data":[]logEntry, total, page, total_pages}.
3. Pagination reads header.Get("X-Next-Page") (absent in v2). Real pagination is body fields page/total_pages. Only page 1 is ever read -> silent drop past page_size. FIX: loop while page < total_pages.
Root cause the tests missed it: internal/meter/litellm/spendsource_test.go mock returns a bare `[ {...} ]` array and ignores the query dates entirely.

=== BUG B (admin update-by-alias, breaks re-provisioning) -- internal/meter/litellm/admin_http.go ===
EnsureKey is idempotent-by-alias: /key/generate on an existing alias returns 400 "Key with alias 'X' already exists" (alreadyExists() matches), then updateByAlias() runs:
1. GET /key/info?key_alias=<alias> returns 404 {"message":"Key not found in database"}. v1.92.0 /key/info accepts ONLY ?key=<token>, NOT ?key_alias=. => EnsureKey errors on the SECOND ensure for any project (every budget change / ReconcileKeys tick / re-register).
2. /key/info shape is nested: {"key":..., "info":{"key_alias":...,"max_budget":...}} -- decodeKeyResponse reads TOP-LEVEL key_alias (would be empty). 
FIX: look the token up another way (LiteLLM has /key/list?key_alias=; or GET /key/info?key=<token> once the token is known; or store the token). Parse the nested .info shape.

=== VERIFIED GOOD (no change needed) ===
- HARD DOOR CLOSES: $1.00 key on glm ($2/1M), 100k tok/call = $0.20; call 6 refused HTTP 429 budget_exceeded "Current cost: 1.0, Max budget: 1.0". Zero overshoot.
- budget_duration "1mo" IS a UTC CALENDAR month: key created 2026-07-19, budget_reset_at 2026-08-01T00:00:00+00:00. (P3-2 OK, not rolling-30-days.)
- /model/info returns input_cost_per_token matching configured prices (qwen 2.5e-07, glm 2e-06, sonnet 6e-06) -> synthetic prices agree, catalog drift checkable (P3-4/P3-8).
- Dedicated proxy-admin key SUFFICES (P3-6): a plain generated key gets 401 on /key/generate & /spend/logs/v2, but a key issued to a /user/new user_role=proxy_admin does all admin calls -> master key NOT required.
- metadata NOT forwarded upstream (stub saw only [messages,model]) -> stub log is a VOLUME check only, attribution must come from v2 spend_logs_metadata.
- /key/delete {"key_aliases":[...]} works, returns {"deleted_keys":[...]}, token refused (401) IMMEDIATELY after.
- Also observed: detailed LiteLLM_SpendLogs table write lag is large/unreliable in single-node podman (rows often not visible within 100s even at proxy_batch_write_at:1; after a proxy restart, completions produced no rows in-window) while the key-level budget counter is immediate. P3-3 (spend-log lag vs max_spend_staleness) must be measured through the real code path AFTER Bug A is fixed.

Evidence + full reproduction in docs/spikes/litellm-verified.md. Blocks Plan 06 Task 5 (L2 suite cannot go green until the adapter speaks v2).
close_reason: Fixed + live-verified against real LiteLLM v1.92.0 + adversarially reviewed (no credential blanking), merged to main (bef6684). Spend poller reads /spend/logs/v2 (YYYY-MM-DD dates, {data,...} envelope, page/total_pages); updateByAlias resolves via /key/list then /key/update; service.go preserves the stored KeyRef on empty token. Mocks rewritten to the real v2 contract. Follow-ups: gonk-4nk, gonk-0qi.

title: Every onboarded project bricks: ReserveIfFits applies cost gate to zero-cost local rungs
description: P0 money-path defect found by Plan 06 L1 (test/integration wiring real intake+meter). The onboarding default ships monthly_cost_usd:0 + ladder:[qwen-local] (local, zero-cost rung; spec 5.3). pkg/rung/decide.go:246 correctly SKIPS the cost gate for zero-cost rungs (if spec.EstCostUSD>0 && !rem.FitsCost). But internal/meter/store/memory.go:146 AND postgres.go:428 apply the cost check UNCONDITIONALLY (if !rem.FitsCost(r.CostUSD)||...), and pkg/budget/remaining.go:119 FitsCost returns false whenever MonthlyCostUSD<=0 regardless of est. So ReserveIfFits asks FitsCost(0) against a $0 ceiling -> false -> rejects a reservation that holds ZERO real dollars, even though Decide just said 'run'. Result: POST /v1/policy/decide returns defer/monthly-cost-exhausted for every freshly-onboarded project -- dead on arrival. Affects BOTH store backends (postgres is the real ledger). Latent because no meter test registered a $0-cost budget with a local ladder. FIX: mirror Decide's gate in both ReserveIfFits impls -> if (r.CostUSD>0 && !rem.FitsCost(r.CostUSD)) || !rem.FitsMonthTokens(r.Tokens) || !rem.FitsTaskTokens(r.Tokens). A zero-cost reservation holds no real dollars so it must always clear the cost leg (token gates still enforce the token budget via synthetic pricing). Add a storetest guard: 'zero-cost local rung reserves under a $0 cost budget'. Money-path -> adversarial review before merge.
close_reason: Fixed + adversarially reviewed + merged to main (8bf5381). Both stores skip the cost leg for zero-cost rungs; verified on real Postgres (fail-before/pass-after, priced rungs still rejected, overspend race 0/10, idempotency intact). Optional future hardening: validateFiniteMoney could also reject CostUSD<0 (unreachable in prod).

title: Prompts are delivered as KEYSTROKES into opencode's TUI; a bang in issue text runs a shell in the agent pod
description:
PROVEN LIVE 2026-08-01, ns gonk.

Gas City delivers a session message with tmux 'send-keys -l' (internal/runtime/carrier.go), i.e. as literal keystrokes into whatever TUI is running in the pane. opencode's composer treats '!' as its SHELL-MODE trigger. So any prompt containing a bang is not asked -- it is EXECUTED.

Reproduction (session go-57b, a healthy live triage pod):
  submitted: 'Hello there, see issue !42 and reply with exactly the word GOLF and nothing else.'
  rendered:  '$ Hello there, see issue 42 and reply with exactly the word GOLF and nothing else.'
             (bang eaten, shell prompt shown)
  produced:  '/bin/sh: 1: Hello: not found'
The model never saw the message at all. Multi-line text, backticks and JSON braces were each tested separately and are FINE -- the bang alone is the trigger, anywhere in the string, not just at position 0.

This was the cause of every wedged triage session: gonk's prompt began '<!-- gonk:model:... -->' and also said 'Triage GitLab issue !18', so the entire prompt ran as a shell command, opencode created an empty session and sat on a spinner forever with no LLM request in its log.

TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS:

1. FUNCTIONAL (mitigated in gonk). cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go now strips '!' from the prompt before submitting (sanitizeForKeystrokeDelivery) and no longer emits the '<!--' marker lines. Verified live: issue 21 produced a real triage analysis and a well-formed GONK_BATCH_START/END fence. Lossy -- exclamation marks and GitLab '!123' MR references do not survive.

2. SECURITY (NOT fixed, and not fixable in gonk alone). The prompt embeds an UNTRUSTED GitLab issue title and body. Stripping bangs closes the observed vector, but the underlying property remains: gonk hands attacker-influenced text to a component that types it into an interactive terminal, where the receiving TUI decides what is a command. Any other input-mode trigger opencode has (or grows) is the same hole. A keystroke channel cannot be made safe by escaping at the sender.

The durable fix is to stop delivering prompts as keystrokes: give the agent its prompt out-of-band and have gonk-agent-entrypoint hand it to opencode directly. That is the same channel gonk-u1p.8 needs for attribution, so the two should be designed together.

UPSTREAM: worth reporting to Gas City that Nudge/SendKeys are a text-injection boundary for any TUI-backed provider, and to opencode that shell mode triggers on a bang anywhere in programmatically-delivered input. DRAFT BOTH, DO NOT POST -- owner reviews and posts (docs/upstream/CONTRIBUTIONS.md).

title: Prompt delivery is silently dropped: deliverPrompt treats the async submit 202 as delivery
description:
PROVEN LIVE 2026-07-31. The gonk-u1p.1 workaround (deliver the prompt as a second signed call) DOES NOT WORK in production, for the same underlying reason as the original bug.

WHAT THE LIVE RUN SHOWED (issue !17, session gonk.triage.p75.i17.a1 / pod go-d3y):
- Full chain fired correctly: POST /order/gonk-dispatch/run 202, POST /sessions 202, POST /session/gonk.triage.p75.i17.a1/submit 202.
- opencode STILL sits at its idle splash. No message, no typed text, nothing.

WHY (gascity @ 4fda5a28, internal/runtime/k8s/provider.go:535):

    func (p *Provider) Nudge(name string, content []runtime.ContentBlock) error {
        _ = p.carrier().Nudge(context.Background(), name, content) // best-effort
        return nil
    }

The carrier's error is DISCARDED and nil is returned unconditionally. SendKeys (line 541) does the same. So when delivery into the pod's tmux session fails, the session Manager sees success, the API answers 202, and the caller is told the message landed. There is no way for gonk -- or any client -- to detect the drop.

So BOTH prompt-delivery mechanisms are broken for k8s-backed sessions, and the second one is silent BY CONSTRUCTION:
  - create-time template_overrides.initial_message -> PromptSuffix, never composed onto the command (gonk-drf / gastownhall/gascity#4891)
  - post-create submit -> Nudge, error swallowed

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SHIPPED FIX: pkg/gcapi.SubmitSession and deliverPrompt are correct and well-tested against the contract, but the contract is not honoured by this backend. The code is not wrong; it cannot work here. Do not revert it -- it is the right shape and becomes correct the moment upstream delivers -- but stop treating it as the unblock.

REMAINING OPTION, now the only viable one without an upstream fix: option (c) from gonk-u1p.1 -- carry the prompt into the pod out-of-band and have gonk-agent-entrypoint feed it to opencode directly (exec opencode --prompt "$(cat /etc/gonk/prompt)" or similar). The entrypoint is OURS, so this needs nothing from Gas City. Open question is the channel: session env is exec-order-only (GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_*), so it likely means a staged file -- note internal/runtime/k8s/staging.go DOES stage files into the pod, which is worth reading before designing this.

Also worth adding to gastownhall/gascity#4891 (or a second report): the swallowed error is arguably the more serious half, because it makes the first bug undiagnosable from the outside.
design: Do NOT 'fix' this by having gonk poll the session output to confirm the prompt arrived and resubmit -- that is a retry loop around a silent failure, and it cannot distinguish 'not delivered' from 'delivered, agent still thinking'. The delivery channel has to be one gonk can actually observe.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatched triage agent visibly receives its prompt in a live k8s session, by a channel whose failure is detectable.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-08-01 by live experiment. The gonk-u1p.7 diagnosis was WRONG on the cause. Three things proven live against ns gonk (session go-d3y / alias gonk.triage.p75.i17.a1):

1. tmux delivery WORKS. Reproducing the carrier's exact two-step by hand --
   'tmux send-keys -t main -l <text>' then 'tmux send-keys -t main Enter' --
   typed into the running opencode TUI and the model answered (PONG, 5.3s over
   LiteLLM). Provider.Nudge swallowing the carrier error is real, but it was
   NOT the failure: the carrier does not fail.

2. SubmitSession WORKS. A probe making the EXACT signed POST
   /v0/city/gonk/session/{alias}/submit that cmd/gonk-gate makes delivered the
   prompt: event request.result.session.submit ok=true session_id=go-d3y
   queued=false, and opencode answered (ALPHA, 498ms). The shipped fix is not
   merely 'correct against the contract' -- it is the unblock.

3. THE ACTUAL BUG IS GONK-SIDE. POST .../submit is fully async: the handler
   returns 202 BEFORE resolving the session, so a submit to a session that does
   not exist yet is answered 202, NOT 404. Proven: submitting to
   gonk.triage.p99.i999.a1 returned 202 and then emitted
     type=request.failed operation=session.submit error_code=resolve_failed
     error_message='session not found: gonk.triage.p99.i999.a1'
   deliverPrompt (cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go) retries ONLY on 404. That
   route never 404s, so the very first submit 'succeeds', dispatch records
   StateRunning, and the prompt is silently dropped whenever the async create
   has not materialized the session yet (a live run took ~31s create->start).
   pkg/gcapi/gcapitest modelled a 404 window that upstream does not have, which
   is why the round-trip test could not catch this.

DETECTION EXISTS. The 202 body carries request_id + event_cursor precisely so
the caller can correlate. GET /v0/city/{city}/events (unsigned, supports
index=<cursor>&wait=30s long-poll) carries the terminal event:
  success: type=request.result.session.submit, payload.request_id
  failure: type=request.failed, payload.{request_id,operation,error_code,error_message}
So the acceptance criterion on this bead is satisfiable without option (c) and
without anything from upstream.

Option (c) (out-of-band prompt file + entrypoint) is NOT needed. Also ruled out
while investigating: session-create 'options' cannot carry the prompt --
ProviderOption is type 'select' only and ResolveExplicitOptions rejects any
value not in the declared choices; and staging (internal/runtime/k8s/staging.go)
is skipped entirely because gonk runs GC_K8S_PREBAKED=true.
close_reason: Closed

title: Declining to judge a running session must not mean waiting forever (reservation is the deadline)
description:
Regression I introduced in the gonk-u1p.2/.5 fix, found on the live cluster within minutes of deploying it.

sweepRunning returned EARLY for a still-running broker session -- before gate.Signals.ReservationExpired was even computed. So a session that never finishes is never reaped: it holds its reservation to TTL and the bead sits in StateRunning permanently with no outcome ever reported.

That is not hypothetical. Session gonk.triage.p75.i16.a2 was created by the PREVIOUS controller image (365518e, which predates the prompt-delivery fix), so its agent never got a prompt and sits at opencode's idle splash. The new sweep correctly declines to judge it -- and would have waited on it forever.

FIX: compute the reservation deadline BEFORE the still-running check. A running session inside its reservation is left alone (correct); a running session PAST its reservation is reaped -- view stays nil so no batch is read, and ReservationExpired classifies it. Covered by TestSweepBrokerReapsARunningSessionPastItsReservation.
acceptance_criteria: A broker session still running past ReservationExpiresAt is classified exactly once rather than waited on indefinitely.

title: Nothing ever stamps SessionEndedAt, so sweep skips every broker bead forever
description:
Found 2026-07-31 while fixing gonk-u1p.2. This is a HARD BLOCKER on the whole triage slice and is independent of the prompt fix.

sweepRunning (cmd/gonk-gate/sweep.go:117) opens with:
    if rec.SessionEndedAt.IsZero() { return }
and NOTHING IN THE TREE EVER SETS SessionEndedAt. grep for an assignment finds exactly one hit -- sweep.go:233, which CLEARS it to the zero value on a re-sling. The field's own doc comment in pkg/beadstore/store.go:66 says it is 'stamped by whatever observes the session finish (Gas City's tracking-id lifecycle, out of this plan's available facts)'. That observer was never built.

CONSEQUENCE: every broker bead sits in StateRunning with a zero SessionEndedAt, so sweepRunning returns on the first line, every 30s, forever. The batch is never read, no outcome is ever reported, no comment is ever posted, and the reservation is left to expire. Tests pass because their fixtures (baseRunningRecord) hand-stamp SessionEndedAt -- the one thing production never does.

This is the third defect in the same untested seam, after gonk-u1p.1 (prompt never delivered) and gonk-u1p.2 (an in-flight session judged as failed). All three are invisible to any test that stubs the session's output instead of modelling its LIFECYCLE, which is what gonk-u1p.4 is for.

FIX (proposed, unifies with gonk-u1p.2): the broker path already fetches the live SessionView, which carries Running/State. That IS the finish signal, and it is more truthful than a field we would have to remember to stamp. For a broker bead (agentForTrigger[trigger] && SessionID != ''), skip the SessionEndedAt precondition and let the live view decide: still running -> ArtifactUnknown, nothing to judge; not running -> read and judge the batch. Stamp SessionEndedAt at that moment so the existing spend-staleness logic (gatherSpend compares cost.AsOf against it) still has its timestamp.

Upstream also emits events.SessionStopped, so a push-based observer is possible later; the live-view read needs no new infrastructure and no event plumbing.
design: Do NOT fix this by stamping SessionEndedAt at dispatch time -- that would make every bead immediately eligible and re-introduce gonk-u1p.2 from the other direction. The stamp must mean 'we observed it finish'. Keep the SessionEndedAt guard for the v1/non-broker path, which has no session view to consult.
acceptance_criteria: A broker bead created by dispatch is picked up by a later sweep with no hand-stamped SessionEndedAt, judged only once its session is no longer running, and its batch applied exactly once.
close_reason: Fixed together with gonk-u1p.2, since both are the same 'is the session done' seam. The broker path no longer gates on SessionEndedAt (which nothing ever stamped); it reads the live session view instead, and stamps SessionEndedAt at the moment it OBSERVES the finish so gatherSpend's staleness comparison still works. The v1/non-broker path keeps the old guard -- it has no session view to consult. Mutation-tested: re-applying the guard to broker beads fails TestSweepBrokerJudgesABeadThatWasNeverStampedEnded.

title: sweep reads the batch without checking the session finished — an in-progress agent is classified as 'no batch' and escalated
description:
Found 2026-07-31 by the owner asking whether we test the session round trip. We do not, and this is what that gap hides.

cmd/gonk-gate/broker_apply.go:82 calls GetSessionOutput(alias, brokerPeekLines) and goes straight to extractBatch(view.LastOutput) at line 93. It NEVER consults view.Running or view.State -- both are parsed into gcapi.SessionView and both are simply unused.

gonk-sweep is a cooldown order with interval=30s. A triage session takes minutes. So the FIRST sweep after dispatch reads a session that is still mid-inference, finds no GONK_BATCH_START/END fence (the agent has not written it yet), and returns violation='no GONK_BATCH_START/END fence in session output'. That folds into gate.Signals with ArtifactPresent=false -> a gate FAILURE -> re-sling, which re-decides and escalates to a MORE EXPENSIVE rung.

In other words: as soon as prompts actually get delivered (gonk-u1p.1, just fixed), essentially EVERY triage run would be marked failed ~30s in and escalated up the ladder while the original agent is still working. It costs money and it corrupts ladder state. We have not seen it only because no agent has ever received a prompt, so no session ever did any work.

FIX: gate the batch read on the session being finished. gcapi.SessionView already carries State and Running. An unfinished session is NOT 'no artifact' -- it is 'not yet known', which must map to signals.ArtifactUnknown (uncertainty must never escalate, AD-6), not to a gate failure.

Upstream also emits real lifecycle events (events.SessionStopped -- 'session.stopped, session.crashed', internal/api/event_payloads.go:626), so reacting to a stop signal is available as a follow-up rather than polling blind. See the sibling bead on reading the transcript.
design: Minimal fix inside applyBrokerBatch: if the view says the session is still running, return a distinct not-finished outcome that the caller maps to ArtifactUnknown rather than to violation/absent. Do NOT reuse the existing 'no fence' violation string for it -- that is the bug. A timeout still needs to exist so a wedged session eventually fails, but it must be a real deadline (e.g. reservation expiry, which sweep already computes) rather than 'the first 30s tick'.
acceptance_criteria: A sweep over a still-running broker session records ArtifactUnknown and does not re-sling; a sweep after the session finishes reads and applies the batch. Both covered by a test.
close_reason: Fixed: sweep now takes the finished/not-finished decision from the LIVE SessionView (Running/State) rather than judging blind. A still-running session returns early -- no classification, no outcome reported, no re-sling -- so a mid-flight agent can no longer be escalated onto a pricier rung. Mutation-tested: removing the running check fails TestSweepBrokerDoesNotJudgeAStillRunningSession.

title: template_overrides.initial_message never reaches opencode — agent session starts idle and never finishes
description:
PROVEN LIVE 2026-07-31 on the first full-stack triage run (issue !16 on project 75, session s-go-nzw, alias gonk.triage.p75.i16.a1). This is exactly the C2 risk the handoff flagged as unproven: 'that template_overrides.initial_message actually reaches opencode as its first prompt'. It does NOT.

WHAT WORKS (all verified this run):
- intake accepts the Issue Hook, project resolves state=valid, gonk_intake_dispatched_total{trigger=issue-triage}=1.
- controller runs the dispatch order: POST /v0/city/gonk/order/gonk-dispatch/run 202.
- ONE signed session create: POST /v0/city/gonk/sessions 202, session s-go-nzw, template=triage, alias gonk.triage.p75.i16.a1 (the correlation marker format from the spec), outcome=success in 31.23s.
- The agent pod runs the new multi-arch image and opencode 1.18.3 comes up healthy, provider wired: the TUI header reads 'Build - qwen3-14b gonk (LiteLLM)'. Model + provider plumbing is GOOD.

WHAT FAILS:
- gc session peek go-nzw shows opencode sitting at its IDLE SPLASH ('Ask anything...') 13+ minutes in. No user message was ever delivered.
- Consequence chain: no prompt -> agent never works -> session stays state=active forever -> gonk-sweep (cooldown 30s) only classifies FINISHED sessions, so it never acts -> no batch, no comment, no labels. Issue !16 still has user_notes_count=0 and no labels.

WHY THIS IS THE WHOLE BALLGAME: the per-issue instruction AND the entire proposed-effects protocol live in the INJECTED prompt (cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go builds the GONK_BATCH_START/END contract and the 'do not post anything yourself' rules). title: [bug] gcapi.ParsePrivateKey TrimSpace corrupts ~4.6% of raw ed25519 keys
description: ParsePrivateKey ran bytes.TrimSpace over RAW ed25519 key material. design: Take exact-length (32 or 64 byte) input VERBATIM; keep bytes.TrimSpace only as the fallback for text files written with a trailing newline. Two new deterministic tests cover every whitespace byte at both ends in both key lengths, plus one proving the trailing-newline text case still parses.

title: Attribution metadata never reaches the agent pod on the submit delivery path
description:
The per-bead attribution metadata (gonk-meter DecideResponse.Metadata) used to ride the prompt as a <!-- gonk:meta:... --> marker line that gonk-agent-entrypoint parsed out of its --prompt argument.

That never worked on this backend and cannot: the k8s runtime provider does not compose PromptSuffix onto the launch command (gastownhall/gascity#4891), so there IS no --prompt. The prompt now arrives by POST .../submit, long after opencode has booted and rendered its overlay from static pod env. A marker delivered that way is unreadable by definition -- and actively harmful, because '<!--' contains a '!', which puts opencode's composer into shell mode and makes the whole prompt execute as a shell command (see gonk-u1p.9).

The markers were therefore removed from the submitted prompt (cmd/gonk-gate/broker_inject.go, renderTriagePrompt). CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: LiteLLM spend rows for agent sessions do NOT carry per-bead attribution. gonk-agent-entrypoint already logs this loudly rather than failing ('spend rows for this session will NOT carry per-bead attribution'), and the model still comes from the chart's static GONK_MODEL, so sessions run -- they are just attributed per-install rather than per-bead. This is a regression against spec goal 4 (attribution at every granularity).

Fixing it needs a real per-session channel into the pod. What is RULED OUT (verified 2026-08-01):
  - session-create 'options': ProviderOption is type 'select' only and ResolveExplicitOptions rejects any value not in the declared choices, so arbitrary text cannot ride it.
  - file staging (internal/runtime/k8s/staging.go): skipped entirely, gonk runs GC_K8S_PREBAKED=true.
  - session env: resolved.Env is static agent/city config; the create API body has no env field.
What IS available: the pod knows its own identity -- GC_ALIAS is in the pod env (verified live: GC_ALIAS=gonk.triage.p75.i17.a1). So the viable design is prompt/metadata BY REFERENCE: gonk stores it keyed by alias and the entrypoint fetches it at startup. The agent pod already has netpol egress to gonk-meter (for GET /v1/cost/session/{key}), which makes gonk-meter the natural place to serve it with no new network surface.

title: Every intake restart silently drops webhooks for up to one reconcile interval
description:
Observed twice on 2026-07-31, both times immediately after a deploy.

On startup intake has no resolved project state, so gonk_intake_projects{state="unsynced"} and every incoming webhook is dropped with gonk_intake_dispatch_dropped_total{reason="state_unsynced"}. State only becomes valid after the reconcile loop runs and gonk-meter resolves the project -- and GONK_RECONCILE_INTERVAL is 10m. So for up to ten minutes after ANY restart (deploy, node move, OOM, crashloop), gonk accepts webhooks with a 200 and throws the work away.

It is silent from the forge's side: GitLab records a successful delivery, the issue is simply never triaged. The only evidence is a counter.

Two contributing wrinkles seen in the same window:
- Intake also races meter at startup (gonk_intake_meter_push_total{result="error"} on the first push, because intake comes up before meter is listening). It recovers on the next reconcile, which is again up to 10m later.
- Nothing re-drives dropped events: a dropped webhook is gone. The issue sits untriaged until something else touches it.

OPTIONS:
 (a) Reconcile once, promptly, on startup (and on meter-push failure) rather than waiting a full interval -- a short retry ladder on boot, e.g. 5s/15s/60s, before settling into the 10m cadence.
 (b) Queue/park events received while unsynced and re-drive them once the project resolves, rather than dropping.
 (c) Both. (a) shrinks the window; (b) makes it lossless.
Recommend (a) first -- it is small and removes most of the exposure.
design: Do NOT fix this by making unsynced dispatch anyway -- unsynced means gonk-meter has not confirmed the project's config, and dispatching on unresolved config would spend against a budget nobody has validated. The correct fix shortens or eliminates the window, it does not lower the bar for entering it.
acceptance_criteria: After an intake restart, a webhook arriving within the first minute is either dispatched or replayed once the project resolves -- not silently dropped.

title: No session round-trip test: launch -> prompt -> session end -> read transcript
description:
Owner question 2026-07-31: 'we don't have a test for the session round trip?' We do not.

WHAT EXISTS: pkg/gcapi unit tests cover CreateSession, SubmitSession and GetSessionOutput INDIVIDUALLY against an httptest fake. cmd/gonk-gate tests drive dispatch and sweep separately against gcapitest, whose SessionOutputs is a pre-seeded map -- the output is placed there by the test, never produced by anything. test/component, test/integration and test/images have no session-lifecycle coverage at all.

WHAT IS MISSING: a test that exercises the actual sequence -- create the session, deliver the prompt, observe the session reach a stopped/ended state, then read the output of record and extract the batch. Every bug in this area so far has lived precisely in the seams that sequence would cross:
  - gonk-u1p.1 (prompt never delivered; the pod launched with a bare command)
  - the sibling bead on classifying an unfinished session as 'no batch'
  - the sibling bead on reading a 400-line preview rather than the transcript
None of the three is visible to a test that stubs the session's output.

TWO LEVELS WORTH BUILDING:
 1. Fake-driven (fast, in CI, no cluster): extend gcapitest to model a session as a STATE MACHINE -- created -> running -> stopped -- with an output that only becomes readable when it stops, and a transcript endpoint distinct from the peek preview. That alone would have caught both sibling bugs.
 2. Live (build-tagged, needs cluster): the real thing against a throwaway namespace, which is gonk-dxo's remaining exit criteria.
design: Level 1 is the priority: it is the cheap, always-run guard, and the state machine is the part that matters -- a fake whose output is a static map cannot express 'not finished yet', which is exactly the condition being got wrong. Model session.stopped explicitly rather than implying it from output presence.
acceptance_criteria: A CI test drives create -> submit -> session-stops -> read and asserts the batch is applied exactly once; it fails if the read happens before the session stops, or if the batch sits beyond the peek window.
close_reason:
Built. gcapitest now models a session LIFECYCLE (running/stopped/crashed) driven by RunSession/FinishSession/CrashSession, instead of a flat output map that could not express 'not finished yet'. An accepted agent create registers the session as RUNNING with no output, so nothing produces a finished session implicitly. peek is modelled as a bounded preview WINDOW and a separate /transcript route returns the whole output, which makes gonk-u1p.3 demonstrable.

TestBrokerRoundTripDispatchToAppliedComment drives the full chain on one fake: dispatch decides + creates + delivers the prompt, a sweep while RUNNING judges nothing, the session finishes with the fenced batch, the next sweep reads/validates/applies exactly one comment + label and reports one success, and a further sweep does not re-apply. Plus a crashed-session case (terminal, so judged, but applies nothing) which the old fake could not express at all.

VERIFIED it earns its keep: reverting gonk-u1p.2 makes it fail with 'sweep judged a running session: outcomes=1'; reverting gonk-u1p.5 makes it fail with 'notes = [], want exactly one triage comment'. Either regression is caught by this one test.

Side benefit: the broker tests no longer sit on gatherSpend's 60s default deadline (SpendPollInterval/SpendDeadline are set short), so the gonk-gate suite runs in ~4s instead of stalling a minute per affected test.

title: broker reads a 400-line peek preview instead of the full session transcript
description:
cmd/gonk-gate/broker_apply.go reads the agent's proposed-effects batch out of GetSessionOutput(alias, brokerPeekLines=400).LastOutput -- a last-output PREVIEW window, not the session's output of record.

The batch must be the LAST thing the agent emits, so a preview usually contains it. But an agent that is chatty after the fence, or that emits a long tool trace, pushes it out of a 400-line window -- and the failure is silent and expensive: no fence found -> gate failure -> re-sling at a pricier rung, with no signal distinguishing 'the agent produced nothing' from 'we did not look far enough'.

Upstream exposes the real thing: GET /v0/city/{city}/session/{id}/transcript (supervisor_city_routes.go:371). Its handler resolves via resolveSessionIDAllowClosedWithConfig, i.e. the transcript is readable even AFTER the session closes -- which the peek path may not be, and which matters because the natural time to read a batch is once the session has ended.

FIX: read the transcript for the batch, keeping peek (if at all) only as a cheap liveness probe. Pair with the sibling bead: wait for finished, then read the transcript.
acceptance_criteria: The batch is extracted from the full transcript, and a test proves a batch preceded by more than brokerPeekLines of agent chatter is still found.
close_reason:
Fixed. The broker now extracts the batch from the session TRANSCRIPT (GET /v0/city/{city}/session/{id}/transcript?tail=0) instead of the bounded peek preview. peek is still used, but only for what it is actually good for: telling us whether the session finished (it carries state/running; the transcript does not).

Modelled on the REAL upstream contract, not a convenient one: sessionTranscriptGetResponse is structured turns ({role,text,timestamp}), not a flat string, and tail=0 means 'all segments' while omitting it returns only the most recent. gcapi.SessionTranscript mirrors that shape and Text() joins turns in order, which preserves extractBatch's last-fence-wins semantics. A paginated response (HasMore) is refused as UNKNOWN rather than judged -- 'no batch' derived from a partial read is the same silent loss in a new costume.

Mutation-tested: reverting to extractBatch(view.LastOutput) fails TestSweepBrokerFindsABatchBuriedBeyondThePeekWindow, which buries the fence under brokerPeekLines+50 lines of trailing chatter.

NOTE the fake's transcript shape was initially INVENTED by me ({id,state,transcript}) and had to be corrected against gascity's source before this landed -- a fake that lies is worse than no fake, since the test would have passed while production failed.

title: Report upstream: Gas City k8s runtime provider drops PromptSuffix/PromptFlag
description:
Gas City's k8s session provider never delivers the startup prompt, so every k8s-backed session boots with no prompt at all.

internal/runtime/runtime.go:660 documents PromptSuffix as 'the shell-quoted prompt text appended to Command when starting the session', with PromptFlag prepended. internal/runtime/acp/acp.go:159-163 implements exactly that, as do the herdr and t3bridge providers. internal/runtime/k8s/pod.go does not: agentCommandB64() base64-encodes cfg.Command verbatim and there is no reference to PromptSuffix or PromptFlag anywhere under internal/runtime/k8s/.

Observed at GASCITY_REF 4fda5a28445f42d6e789fc7f5751645ac4fecd19. A live session pod's command decoded to the bare start_command with no arguments, and the agent sat at its idle TUI splash indefinitely.

Affects both the rendered template prompt and template_overrides.initial_message, since cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go:1100 routes the latter onto the same PromptSuffix field.

Suggested fix is a direct port of the acp composition into agentCommandB64 (or its caller), taking care that the result is still safely shell-quoted for the tmux 'CMD=$(echo ... | base64 -d)' wrapper and for buildRespawnCommand, which must stay byte-identical to the entrypoint launch.

Mirrors gonk-wgq (the LiteLLM /spend/logs DoS) as an upstream report we owe back.
acceptance_criteria: An upstream issue or PR exists against gastownhall/gascity describing the k8s provider prompt drop, with the acp composition cited as the reference implementation.
notes:
EVIDENCE + IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (gascity @ 4fda5a28, read 2026-07-31):

GAS CITY'S OWN INTENDED CONTRACT:
- cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go:1100 puts the template prompt AND template_overrides.initial_message onto runtime.Config.PromptSuffix (with PromptFlag).
- internal/runtime/runtime.go:660 documents PromptSuffix as 'the shell-quoted prompt text APPENDED TO COMMAND when starting the session'.
- The PROVIDER is responsible for that composition. tmux (adapter.go:1392 buildLaunchCommand), acp (acp.go:159), herdr and t3bridge all do it. internal/runtime/k8s does NOT -- zero references to PromptSuffix/PromptFlag.

WHY IT WAS NEVER CAUGHT: the Phase-2 worker conformance matrix (cmd/gc/template_resolve_phase2_test.go) covers profiles claude/tmux-cli, codex/tmux-cli, gemini/tmux-cli, kimi/tmux-cli, opencode/tmux-cli, mimocode/tmux-cli, antigravity/tmux-cli -- EVERY profile is tmux-cli. There is NO k8s profile. WC-INPUT-001 (initial message on first start) is asserted against cfg.PromptSuffix, i.e. at the runtime.Config level, so it passes even for a provider that never delivers the field. opencode is conformance-tested on tmux-cli; opencode on k8s is not covered at all.

THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINE CONCAT. tmux's buildLaunchCommand has a size branch: maxInlinePromptLen = 1024 (adapter.go:1384). Above that it writes a prompt FILE and returns longPromptCommand(), an 'sh -c' script that cats the file into a variable and execs the agent with it -- with an explicit comment that the inline path otherwise triggers ENAMETOOLONG / exit 126 / 'File name too long' tmux pane death. This matters directly for k8s because the k8s provider ALSO wraps the command in tmux (tmux new-session -d -s main "$CMD"), and gonk's injected prompt carries up to 8KiB of issue context -- 8x over the inline limit. A naive concatenation in agentCommandB64 would produce exactly the failure that helper exists to prevent.

VIABLE k8s IMPLEMENTATION: the provider already has CopyTo (provider.go:673) which tars a local file into the pod at /workspace. So the file-based path is achievable: write the prompt file, CopyTo it into the pod, and emit the longPromptCommand form. Note buildRespawnCommand must stay byte-identical to the entrypoint launch (the code says so explicitly), so both paths need the same treatment.

NOT A DECLARED LIMITATION: k8s Provider.Capabilities() (provider.go:661) reports only CanReportActivity; nothing declares prompt delivery unsupported. This is an unimplemented path, not a documented constraint.

title: Confirm New() and NewServer() bridge nodes are Go constructor-naming artifacts, not architecture

These are near-certainly an artifact of Go's constructor naming convention: every package has its own unrelated New(), and the extractor collapsed them into one node because the node ID was built from the symbol name rather than a fully package-qualified path. They bridge the meter, intake, gate and harness layers only because those layers each happen to define a function with the same name.

This matters for graph trust, not for the code: if confirmed, the top two 'core abstractions' in the God Nodes list are noise, and the same likely applies to Render(), Minimum(), MustObject(), Server, Service and Request.

Do NOT refactor any Go code on the basis of this. The fix, if wanted, is on the graphify extraction side (package-qualified node IDs).
design: Check the node IDs behind New()/NewServer() in graphify-out/graph.json and confirm whether multiple distinct package-level constructors were merged into one node. Cross-check against the 1427 dangling-endpoint edges from the health gate - both may share a node-ID normalisation root cause.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed as an extraction artifact (or not). If artifact, the God Nodes section of GRAPH_REPORT.md is annotated as unreliable and gonk-fm7's caveat is updated.
